sources.title: Form 10-K for fiscal 2025
sources.text: Net sales were $1.24 billion, up 11% from $1.12 billion, led by cordless power tools, which grew 19%. Gross margin improved to 38.5% from 36.9% as steel and freight costs eased. The company opened a second assembly plant in Monterrey, Mexico, in September. Risk factors note that its three largest retail customers account for 46% of net sales.

sources.title: Form 10-Q for the first quarter of fiscal 2026
sources.text: Quarterly net sales were $301 million, up 7%. Inventory rose to $412 million from $355 million at year end, which management attributes to stocking the new plant. Long-term debt was unchanged at $280 million.

sources.title: Risewell recalls 40,000 cordless drills over battery overheating
sources.text: Risewell Tools said it is voluntarily recalling about 40,000 cordless drills sold since March after 12 reports of battery packs overheating, with no injuries reported. The company estimated the cost of the recall at $9 million to $12 million and said a supplier's cell batch was the cause.

sources.title: Form 10-K for fiscal 2025
sources.text: Revenue was flat at $3.05 billion as price increases of 4% offset a 4% decline in volume. Operating margin fell to 9.1% from 10.4%, mainly from higher wheat and packaging costs. The company paid $180 million in dividends and bought back $60 million of its shares.

sources.title: Form 8-K: chief executive transition
sources.text: The board appointed Dana Ruiz, previously chief operating officer, as chief executive officer effective June 1, 2026, succeeding Lee Park, who will retire after nine years in the role and remain an adviser through the end of the year.

sources.title: Flatland Foods to close two bakeries in plant consolidation
sources.text: Flatland Foods will close bakeries in Toledo and Fresno by early 2027 and move production to its larger plants, a change it expects to save $35 million a year after one-time costs of about $50 million.
